text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Comprehensive diabetic foot program: foot inspection, monofilament and vibration testing, and pulses at every visit; IWGDF risk category 2 with podiatry every three months for callus and nail care; protective daily shoes and low-heeled custom stage shoes; daily self-inspection with a magnifying mirror or her dresser's help; and same-day care for any blister, wound, or color change
  • Vascular surgery consultation for claudication with an ankle-brachial index of 0.62: arterial duplex, supervised exercise therapy, and whether and when revascularization should be considered, before any loss of tissue
  • Hypoglycemia safety on tour: glipizide stopped; glargine reduced 20% and moved to the morning, at a fixed clock time with written time-zone steps; a continuous glucose monitor with low alerts shared, with her consent, with her road manager; a glucose check before each show and a meal before late shows; glucose tablets in the dressing room and at the side of the stage; nasal glucagon with the road manager trained; and the beta-blocker's effect on warning signs explained
  • Glucose-lowering medicines with heart and kidney benefit: empagliflozin 10 mg started, with sick-day rules (hold on days she cannot eat or drink and before surgery), genital hygiene advice, and a foot check at each visit; metformin continued with vitamin B12 checked; A1c every three months until at goal (goal below 7.5%)
  • Cardiovascular protection: atorvastatin raised to 80 mg with a lipid panel 4 to 12 weeks later and a goal LDL below 55 mg/dL; aspirin and metoprolol continued; blood pressure goal below 130/80 mmHg
  • Eye care: retina clinic appointment within two weeks for the right macular edema, for anti-VEGF injections; retinal examination of both eyes at least yearly and more often while being treated; large-print materials
  • Kidney and laboratory monitoring: creatinine, eGFR and potassium at three months and then every six to twelve months, urine albumin-creatinine ratio yearly, liver tests after the statin change if symptoms, and vitamin B12 periodically on metformin
  • Access and equity: scheduling around tour dates, video visits on the road, large-print instructions, drug-cost checks before prescribing, coordination with clinics in tour cities, and diabetes self-management education and medical nutrition therapy timed to her touring
  • Supervised exercise therapy for claudication: treadmill walking to moderate calf pain, 30 to 45 minutes three times a week for twelve weeks at a hospital program, with a structured home walking plan for tour weeks; then walking at least three times a week for life
  • Low-dose rivaroxaban 2.5 mg twice daily with aspirin 81 mg to lower the risk of heart attack, stroke, and major limb events, with bleeding precautions and no anti-inflammatory painkillers
  • Revascularization plan: no procedure now; endovascular treatment of the right superficial femoral artery to be considered if claudication still limits her life after twelve weeks of supervised exercise and medical therapy; urgent vascular review for rest pain, a wound, or color change; ankle-brachial index and duplex at six months
  • Semaglutide 0.25 mg weekly for four weeks, then 0.5 mg weekly, for cardiovascular benefit and walking distance, with the retina clinic told before the start because a fast fall in glucose can briefly worsen retinopathy; ezetimibe 10 mg added for an LDL of 64 mg/dL

resource.title: Ella Fitzgerald synthetic care plan
resource.description: Limb-, sight- and heart-protecting primary care for a 70-year-old touring singer with type 2 diabetes, peripheral artery disease with claudication, diabetic macular edema, and coronary bypass surgery the year before: the comprehensive diabetic foot examination (inspection, 10-g monofilament, vibration, pulses) with the ankle- and toe-brachial indices, IWGDF risk grading and a high-risk foot program with podiatry and stage footwear; prompt vascular surgery evaluation, supervised exercise therapy, and a clear plan for revascularization if symptoms limit her life; a high-intensity statin with ezetimibe to an LDL below 55 mg/dL, aspirin with low-dose rivaroxaban, and glucose-lowering medicines with cardiovascular and kidney benefit (empagliflozin, then semaglutide) in place of a sulfonylurea; retinal care with anti-VEGF injections; kidney monitoring; hypoglycemia safety on tour (insulin timing across time zones, a continuous glucose monitor, glucagon, and a show-day plan); and the equity and access steps that make this care reach her, on the ADA Standards of Care 2026, the IWGDF 2023 guidelines, the 2024 ACC/AHA lower extremity PAD guideline, and the CMID diabetes monograph.
